questions.question: The value of an article depreciated from Rs. 18,000 to Rs. 14,580 in 2 years. Find the yearly rate of depreciation in the value of the article.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Initial Value (V1) = Rs. 18,000

Final Value after 2 years (V2) = Rs. 14,580

Time (t) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

The formula for depreciation (when depreciation rate is constant) is given by:

V2 = V1 times (1 - r/100)^t

 r = 100 × (1 - (V2/V1)⁽¹/t⁾⁾ [IMAGE: data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAPABAP///wAAACH5BAEKAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAICRAEAOw==] [IMAGE: data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAPABAP///wAAACH5BAEKAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAICRAEAOw==] 

Where:

V2 is the final value,

V1 is the initial value,

r is the rate of depreciation (in percentage),

t is the time (in years).

Calculation:

r = 100 × (1 - (V2/V1)⁽¹/t⁾⁾ [IMAGE: data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAPABAP///wAAACH5BAEKAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAICRAEAOw==] [IMAGE: data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAPABAP///wAAACH5BAEKAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAICRAEAOw==] 

⇒ r = 100 × (1 - (14580 / 18000)⁽¹/²⁾⁾

⇒ r = 100 × (1 - (0.81)⁰.⁵

⇒ r = 100 × (1 - 0.90)

⇒ r = 10 %

So, the yearly rate of depreciation is approximately 10%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

 For Depreciation

Amount = Principal(1 - rate/100)Time

14580 = 18000(1 - rate/100)²

⇒ 14580/18000 = (1 - rate/100)²

⇒ √(1458/1800) = 1 - rate/100 

⇒ 9/10 = 1 - rate/100

⇒ rate/100 = 1 - 9/10

⇒ rate = 10%

∴ The yearly rate of depreciation in the value of the article is 10%

questions.question: Ramu and Mohan can separately complete a work in 10 hours and 16 hours, respectively. After working for 2 hours together, Mohan leaves the work. In how many hours will Ramu finish the remaining work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ramu can complete the work in 10 hours.

Mohan can complete the work in 16 hours.

**Concept Used:**

Work = Time × Efficiency

**Calculation:**

Total work = LCM(10, 16) = 80 units

Efficiency of Ramu = 80/10 = 8

Efficiency of Mohan = 80/16 = 5

When they work together, their combined efficiency is:

⇒ 8 + 5 = 13

They work together for 2 hours, so the amount of work they complete is:

⇒ 2 × 13 = 26 units

Remaining work = 80 - 26 = 54 units

Days taken by Ramu complete the remaining work = 54/8 = 6.75 hours

**Therefore, Ramu will finish the remaining work in 6.75 hours.**

questions.question: A car covers a certain distance in 3 h with a speed of 108 km/h. If the speed is reduced by 27 km/h, then the time taken by the car to cover the same distance will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed = 108 km/h

Time = 3 h

**Formula:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Solution:**

The distance covered by the car is 108 × 3 = 324 km.

If the speed is reduced by 27 km/h, the new speed is 108 - 27 = 81 km/h.

The new time taken by the car to cover the same distance is 324/81 = 4 h.

Therefore, the time taken by the car to cover the same distance will be 4 h.

**The answer is 4 h.**

**Therefore, the average speed for the entire journey is 3.43 km/h.**

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 8 days and B in 24 days. They begin together, but 4 days before the completion of the work, A leaves. Find the number of days taken by A and B to complete the entire work.
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

We can calculate the number taken to complete the work using the formula

Days = y(x + n)/(x + y)

Where x and y are the number of days taken by A and B.

And n is the number of days before A left

Here we have x = 8, y = 24 and n = 4

Hence, days required = 24 × (8 + 4)/(8 + 24)

= 24 × 12/32

= 9 days

**∴ Option 3 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: A thief started his journey at a speed of 60 km/h. After 30 minutes, police started from the same place but at a speed of 80 km/h. How much time (in hours) will the police take to catch the thief?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Thief's initial speed (Vt) = 60 km/h

Police's speed (Vp) = 80 km/h

Time elapsed before police starts (T) = 30 minutes = 0.5 hours

**Formula:**

Distance (D) = Speed (V) × Time (T)

**Solution:**

Let the time take by police to catch the thief is t.

t = (60 km/h × 0.5)/(80 km/h - 60 km/h)

t = (30 km/h)/(20 km/h)

t = 3/2 hr

**Therefore, the police will take 3/2 hours to catch the thief.**

questions.question: The curved surface area of a sphere is 1386 cm². The volume of this sphere is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The curved surface area of a sphere is 1386 cm2.

**Formula used:**

Surface area of a sphere with radius ‘r’ = 4πr2

Volume of sphere is 4/3 π r3

**Calculation:**

Surface area of a sphere with radius ‘r’ = 4πr2

⇒ 4 × 22/7 × r2 = 1386

⇒ r2 = 110.25

⇒ r = √110.25 = 10.5 cm

Volume of sphere is 4/3 π r³

4/3π(10.5)3

4/3 × 22/7 × 21/2 × 21/2 × 21/2

4851 cm3

**∴ Option 2 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: The price of petrol is raised to Rs. 96.5 per litre from Rs.92 per litre. What is the percentage increase in price of petrol?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The initial price of petrol = Rs. 92 per litre

New price of petrol = Rs. 96.5 per litre

**Formula:**

Percentage increase = ((New value - Initial value)/Initial value) × 100

**Solution:**

Percentage increase = ((96.5 - 92)/92) × 100

(4.5/92) × 100 = 4.9%

**Therefore, the percentage increase in the price of petrol is 4.9%.**

questions.question: The third proportional to 24 and 36 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The third proportional to any two numbers a and b is given directly by the formula: b² ÷ a.

Here, a = 24 and b = 36.

Third proportional = (36 × 36) ÷ 24

Third proportional = 1296 ÷ 24 = 54

**∴ The correct answer is 54.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Two numbers: 24 and 36

**Formula Used:**

If x is the third proportional to a and b, then the ratio is defined as a : b :: b : x

Product of extremes = Product of means

⇒ a × x = b × b

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/517a48539f11fb70bb7db2928970f558fd0119d43202c4998f37e4b066dda572.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the third proportional be x.

⇒ 24 : 36 = 36 : x

⇒ 24 ÷ 36 = 36 ÷ x

⇒ x = (36 × 36) ÷ 24

⇒ x = 1296 ÷ 24

⇒ x = 54

**∴ The correct answer is 54.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fourth Proportional

If a, b, c, and d are in proportion (a : b :: c : d), then d is called the fourth proportional. Formula: d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is the square root of their product. Formula: Mean proportional = √(a × b).

Third Proportional

The third proportional to a and b is a value x such that a : b :: b : x. Formula: x = b² ÷ a.

Continued Proportion

Three quantities a, b, and c are in continued proportion if a : b = b : c. Here b is the mean proportional and c is the third proportional.

questions.question: Under a discount scheme, after allowing a discount of 20%, there is still a gain of 10%. The marked price is what percentage more than the cost price?
questions.solution:
Given:

A discount of 20%, there is still a gain of 10%.

**Formula used:**

MP/CP = (100 + profit%)/(100 - discount%)

Calculation:

MP/CP = (100 + profit%)/(100 - discount%)

MP/CP = (110)/(80)

MP/CP = (11)/(8)

According to the question:

11 - 8 = 3

3/8 × 100 = 37.5%

∴ Option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Harshi bought a new sweatshirt at the store, when they were giving a 40 percent discount. If the marked price of the sweatshirt was Rs. 2999, then how much did Harshi pay with the discount?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked price of the sweatshirt = Rs. 2999

Discount percentage = 40%

**Formula:**

Amount to be paid after discount = Marked price - (Discount percentage × Marked price)/100

**Solution:**

Substituting the given values into the formula:

2999 - (40/100) × 2999

2999 - (0.4) × 2999

2999 - 1199.6

Rs. 1799.40

**Therefore, Harshi paid Rs. 1799.40 after applying the 40% discount on the marked price.**

questions.question: A man sold two chairs for Rs. 475 each, gaining 25% on one and losing 20% on the other. Had he sold the two chairs for Rs. 575 each, what would have been his gain/loss percentage (rounded off to the nearest integer)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

CP₁ = 475 × (100 ÷ 125) = ₹380 & CP₂ = 475 × (100 ÷ 80) = ₹593.75

Total CP = 380 + 593.75 = ₹973.75

Total New SP = 575 × 2 = ₹1150

Gain % = [(1150 − 973.75) ÷ 973.75] × 100

Gain % = (176.25 ÷ 973.75) × 100 ≈ 18%

**∴ The correct answer is 18% gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling price of 1st chair = ₹475, Profit = 25%

Selling price of 2ⁿd chair = ₹475, Loss = 20%

New selling price of each chair = ₹575

 

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price = [SP × 100] ÷ (100 ± Profit/Loss %)

Profit % = [Total Profit ÷ Total Cost Price] × 100

 
 
 CP1 = ₹380 
 +25% Profit SP1 = ₹475 CP2 = ₹593.75 
 -20% Loss SP2 = ₹475 
• Total CP ₹973.75 
 New Scenario Gain ≈ 18% Total New SP ₹1150 

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP of 1st chair = 475 × (100 ÷ 125) = ₹380

⇒ CP of 2ⁿd chair = 475 × (100 ÷ 80) = ₹593.75

⇒ Total Cost Price = 380 + 593.75 = ₹973.75

⇒ Total New Selling Price = 575 × 2 = ₹1150

⇒ Total Gain = 1150 − 973.75 = ₹176.25

⇒ Gain % = (176.25 ÷ 973.75) × 100

⇒ Gain % = 18.099% ≈ 18%

**∴ The correct answer is 18% gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Overall Profit/Loss with Same SP

When two items are sold at the same selling price, one at a profit of x% and the other at a loss of x%, there is always an overall loss given by (x² ÷ 100)%.

Successive Profit/Loss

When an article's price undergoes multiple percentage changes successively, the net effect can be found using the formula: x + y + (xy ÷ 100)%.

Dishonest Dealer

If a trader claims to sell goods at CP but uses false weight, his Profit % = [(True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight] × 100.
